paper.title: Profiling of chromatin accessibility identifies transcription factor binding sites across the genome of Aspergillus species
paper.authors: Huang L, Li X, Dong L, Wang B, Pan L.
paper.association_evidence: Methods: 'sequenced at BGI with 50 bp single-end reads on the BGISEQ-500 (NCBI accession number, PRJNA588127)'.

study_summary.objective: Map open chromatin (ATAC-seq) in A. niger and A. oryzae to find transcription factor binding sites, and test how the regulator LaeA changes secondary-metabolism gene clusters in A. oryzae.
study_summary.experimental_design: A. oryzae niaD300 wild type and its laeA deletion and overexpression mutants were grown to mid-log phase (DPY medium assumed), 2 biological replicates each, with RNA-seq on the mycelium left from ATAC-seq (BGISEQ-500, 50 bp single end).
study_summary.main_finding: laeA deletion and overexpression changed chromatin accessibility at 164 and 138 secondary-metabolism genes and the expression of 32 and 42 of them, but only for clusters already expressed in the wild type, never switching on silent ones.

dpy_flask.note: 2% glucose, 1% peptone, 0.5% yeast extract, 0.5% KH2PO4, 0.05% MgSO4; the paper says DPY or a conditional induction medium for these cultures
liquid culture, mycelium filtered with Miracloth

tags.note: niaD300 is the reference strain of the study

notes: Temperature and time are not stated, and the text does not say whether the A. oryzae cultures used DPY or the conditional induction medium; DPY is assumed.
A figure legend calls the two replicates 'technical' while the text calls them biological; they are treated as biological replicates.
The BioProject also holds A. niger runs (CBS513.88, SH2 and transcription-factor deletions), which are outside the atlas.
